scope: KI and TO; finished factory-sealed 100 g Japanese Camellia sinensis sencha, steamed/rolled/dried, bought for private consumption and posted from Japan. No special permits/certificates/registrations/advance notice; ordinary Customs/arrival declarations allowed.

internationalEvidence.locator: ISPM 32 section 2 and Appendix 2, printed p.32-14 / PDF p.16
internationalEvidence.finding: Tea is expressly illustrated as Category 1. Appendix is reference material; the standard does not cover contaminating/storage pests acquired after processing, and does not itself issue a national import specification or repeal a national permit provision.

operativeText.finding: Manufactured plant products included unconditionally, with all such products regulated articles.
Permit/certificate only if required by specifications; Director must assess risk, use reasonably necessary measures, have regard to SPS/international standards and may apply precaution.
Written pre-import application required only when no specification already exists.
Individual written exemption requires advance request; not automatic.
Office/register publication and preserved compatible legacy specifications preclude inferring no specification merely from no online result.

KI.whyISPMDoesNotClose: Mandatory regard is not mandatory automatic incorporation. The statutory process expressly requires a specification for regulated manufactured articles, regardless of their risk category. A general published specification could suffice; tea-specific naming or bespoke authority ruling is not demanded.
KI.foodLayer: Food Regulations2014 section56 personal-food exemption <=10 kg retained. No independent special-food-paperwork obstacle inferred.
KI.genuineGap: The existing section 26 specification or compatible saved legacy instrument applicable to factory-sealed manufactured Camellia tea: does it permit ordinary postal arrival clearance alone, or impose special permits/certificates? The Act’s mandatory consideration of international standards does not itself answer that question; if no specification exists, section 27 requires advance written application.

operativeText.finding: Plant excludes manufactured items, but separate plant material category includes all materials of plant origin; import covers any conveyance and person includes individuals.
Repealed by Act10/1995, correcting earlier source age.
Affirmative written-permit duty for any plant, plant material or other regulated article.
Mail expressly within inspection/opening and Customs/Post Office hold/notification provisions.

Specified no-permit preserved fruit/vegetable concessions exist; Reg26 requires permits for manufactured material assessed by Director as serious exotic-pest carrier but contains no express exemption for other manufactured material.

TO.inferenceLevel: Conservative legal-scope inference, not explicit national tea ruling.
TO.counterargumentConsidered: One might infer Reg26 intends to limit manufactured-material permits to Director-assessed risks. The current parent Act25(1), however, separately states a broad duty; Reg26 lacks only/except language or an express general waiver. The proposal retains this interpretive caveat and does not present the Act as an unqualified tea-specific authority determination.
TO.whyISPMDoesNotClose: No general mandatory incorporation of ISPM32 was found in this Act or these Regulations; certificate-format references are narrower. Category1 technical treatment therefore cannot nullify the current positive statutory permit duty.
TO.certificateCaution: Do not rely on Act25(2) living-plants-and-plant-material wording to assert a foreign phytosanitary certificate is required for finished tea; permit alone is the proposed blocker.
TO.foodLayer: Existing private/commercial distinction under FoodAct2020 retained; no independent private-food certificate blocker added.
